name: VRchaeology
shortDescription: An immersive virtual field school for learning archaeological field methods through excavation, mapping, documentation, and analysis.

heroMedia.alt: VRchaeology cover art: an illuminated cave waterfall and bridge, with the VRchaeology title and Game Studies and Design, The stu/dio mark.

body:
## Ready for the classroom

VRchaeology is ready for classroom use. Development continues at the Game Studies and Design (GSD) Stu/dio, with work on new labs and improvements to the experience.

[Ask about classroom use](/join/#classroom-use)

## Learning through fieldwork

VRchaeology teaches archaeological field methods using immersive virtual reality, allowing students to learn archaeology without leaving the classroom. It serves as a test case for field sciences more broadly.

Students set up research grids, locate artifacts, map features, excavate, photograph finds, and run lab analyses. The experience is built in Unreal Engine.

## Project history

First taught as ANTH 399, the virtual field school began with 15 undergraduates working in pairs. Its virtual cave is modeled partly on a real cave excavated in the 1930s. Students transferred skills to real excavations.

The original team included Laura Shackelford, Wen-Hao David Huang, and Cameron Merrill. The work was presented at the Society for Historical Archaeology meeting in Boston in 2020.

## Project strands

- Archaeology Lab Class
- Field School Prep
- Virtual Reality for Wheelchair Users

## Teaching

GSD 282: VRchaeology, Spring 2027, was co-created by Laura Shackelford and Sepehr Vaez Afshar.

## Support

National Science Foundation awards 1736235 and 2021460, and Epic MegaGrants.
